text: Forty territories would mean forty static roles. Dynamic RLS solves that with just one.
One role, one filter, adapting to whoever's actually signed in — matched against a small user-mapping table you add to the model.
Here's the classic bug: USERNAME and USERPRINCIPALNAME return different formats in Desktop versus the service. Your mapping table has to match the service's format, not what you saw while testing.
Test as role validates the filter logic. Select it from the role's More options — you're redirected to the underlying report, since dashboards can't be tested this way.
Now viewing as lets you test a role, a combination, or a specific person. But remember: it still runs the dynamic function using your own identity, not theirs.
That's the whole pattern working. Lesson 83 covers what happens when RLS meets a genuinely complex model — bidirectional relationships and beyond.
